turns.en: But actually, so on a serious note, if you think about the AI trade, I mean, the sun around which it all revolves is NVIDIA, both in terms of like providing the actual chips that powers a lot of this technology and also providing a lot of the financing and investments for these companies. Yeah. And so any hint of a scandal has big implications for AI as a whole.
turns.zh: 不过说正经的，如果你想想 AI 交易（AI trade），整个体系围绕它旋转的那个太阳就是 NVIDIA——它既提供驱动这些技术的实际芯片，也为这些公司提供大量的融资和投资。是的。所以任何一点丑闻的苗头，对整个 AI 来说影响都很大。

turns.en: No, I really like the way you put that, that they are the son of the universe. Both from it, they have the crown jewel technology, the chips. They have the financing to back all kinds of partners and neoclouds and everything all around the world.
turns.zh: 不，我真的很喜欢你这个说法——他们是这个宇宙的太阳。一来，他们手里握着皇冠上的明珠那项技术，也就是芯片；二来，他们有钱去支持全球各地的各种合作伙伴、新型云服务商（neocloud）等等。

turns.en: Everyone wants it.
turns.zh: 人人都想要。

turns.en: And it is a technology that is both commercially intensely in demand and geopolitically in demand. And so in addition to the fact that the tech is good and they have the financing, there are all these fights about who they could even sell it to starting, you know, there are all these things of the Biden administration, lobbying of the Trump administration, how liberal should the policies be about who gets to buy them, et cetera. That is why this story is just like, so it's huge.

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And just on the geopolitical, atomic's a good word. On the geopolitical angle itself, I mean, there's this tension that we've seen more and more in recent years where some people will argue that, well, you want the U.S., you want a company like NVIDIA to be the backbone of like the AI tech stack, right? And so maybe you want lots of people using their chips.
turns.zh: 而且单就地缘政治这个角度——这个词用得挺妙。近几年我们越来越常看到这样一种张力：有些人会说，你希望美国、希望像 NVIDIA 这样的公司成为整个 AI 技术栈（AI tech stack）的骨架，对吧？那你可能就希望很多人都在用它的芯片。

turns.en: Totally, totally.
turns.zh: 完全同意，完全同意。

turns.en: But on the other hand, you know, you have people in the Trump administration who argue that we are in this existential AI race with China, and therefore it's really important that China does not have access to the most advanced chips. And so we're seeing that sort of play out in a lot of the discussion on what's going on with NVIDIA right now.
turns.zh: 但另一方面，Trump 政府里也有人主张，我们正处在一场与中国之间关乎存亡的 AI 竞赛中，因此绝不能让中国拿到最先进的芯片。所以现在围绕 NVIDIA 事态的很多讨论，其实就是这种张力在上演。

turns.en: The other thing that's very important, and this will allow us to get into the guest, is that in some sense, there's actually, like, the story's kind of old news, right? There's been a lot of reporting on this company, Megaspeed, and its CEO, and the company's closeness to NVIDIA and Jensen specifically, and where they know. So, like, in a way, like, what is the new news here is part of the question, but whatever, you know. I guess on some level, the new news... is just specifically Jensen Wong admitting to NVIDIA that he had this relationship, an affair, with this executive or someone associated with Megaspeed and the investigation into it. Anyway, without further ado, we really do have the perfect guest, someone who I think is like the best beat in the world. Whenever we get a chance to chat, I'm always learning more about both the sort of like politics, geopolitics of chip flows and, around the world, someone who's reported on chips all around the world, from D.C. to San Francisco, and now based in Hong Kong. We're going to be speaking with tech reporter here at Bloomberg News, Mackenzie Hawkins. So, Mackenzie, thank you so much for coming on Odd Lots.
turns.zh: 还有一点很重要，也能帮我们引出今天的嘉宾：某种意义上，这件事其实已经不算新闻了，对吧？关于 Megaspeed 这家公司、它的 CEO、它跟 NVIDIA 特别是跟 Jensen 的密切关系，以及他们都认识谁，已经有大量报道了。所以说，'新'在哪儿本身就是问题的一部分，不过算了。我想在某个层面上，新的东西……具体就是 Jensen Huang 向 NVIDIA 承认他跟 Megaspeed 的一位高管或者相关人员有这段关系、这段婚外情，以及随之而来的调查。好了，废话不多说，我们今天真的请到了最合适的嘉宾——我认为她跑的是全世界最好的这条线。每次有机会跟她聊，我都能对芯片在全球流动背后的政治、地缘政治了解更多；她在世界各地报道过芯片，从 D.C. 到 San Francisco，现在常驻 Hong Kong。我们要对话的是 Bloomberg News 的科技记者 Mackenzie Hawkins。Mackenzie，非常感谢你来上 Odd Lots。

turns.zh: 非常感谢你们邀请我。这一周可真够呛。

turns.zh: 你在 Hong Kong，还要熬夜来上 Odd Lots，所以真的谢谢你。

turns.en: I can't believe how fried you must be. So again, thank you for taking the time. Let me start with this question. You know, reporters always think they know a little bit more than what they can write at any given moment, etc.
turns.zh: 我都不敢想你现在的脑子有多糊。再次感谢你抽出时间。我先问这么一个问题：记者在任何时候知道的，其实总比能写出来的要多一点，等等。

turns.zh: 假设我们是一周前在聊。

What was the answer you gave me a week ago? Just that you're totally able, who is Megaspeed? And why should we care about this company called Megaspeed?
turns.zh: 那么只根据你当时被允许报道的内容——假设这段对话发生在 10 月的某个时候，我们问：Mackenzie，Megaspeed 这家公司到底是怎么回事？一周前你会怎么回答我？就是那种你完全可以公开说的：Megaspeed 是谁？我们为什么要关心这家叫 Megaspeed 的公司？

turns.en: So pre-affair admission, Megaspeed is the single largest Southeast Asian buyer of NVIDIA chips. It's a major supplier of AI compute to Alibaba. which is one of the most important tech companies and frontier AI leaders in China. It purchased $ 4. 6 billion worth of NVIDIA hardware after being spun off from a Chinese gaming company, passing through a BVI shell, and incorporating in Singapore, then becoming an official NVIDIA partner four days later. Its executive had a close relationship with Jensen. We didn't know quite how close. And it had been under U.S. investigation and Singapore investigation for, if we're talking a week ago, at least a year.
turns.zh: 那么在'婚外情'被承认之前，Megaspeed 是东南亚最大的 NVIDIA 芯片买家。它是 Alibaba 的重要 AI 算力供应商，而 Alibaba 是中国最重要的科技公司之一、也是前沿 AI 的领军者之一。这家公司从一家中国游戏公司分拆出来、经过一个 BVI（英属维尔京群岛）空壳、在 Singapore 注册成立，随后采购了价值 46 亿美元的 NVIDIA 硬件，并在注册成立四天后成为 NVIDIA 的官方合作伙伴。它的一位高管跟 Jensen 关系密切，我们当时还不知道有多密切。而且如果我们说的是一周前，它已经接受美国方面和新加坡方面的调查至少一年了。

turns.en: So why did this raise eyebrows in the first place? So Megaspeed renting out GPU capacity to a company like Alibaba. My understanding is like, OK, that's allowed. People know that this is happening. But at the same time, if you're worried about Chinese companies having access to technologically advanced NVIDIA chips, it seems like a pretty big loophole.
turns.zh: 那这件事一开始为什么会引起警觉？Megaspeed 把 GPU 算力租给 Alibaba 这样的公司，我的理解是：好，这是允许的，大家也都知道有这种事在发生。但同时，如果你担心中国公司能拿到技术先进的 NVIDIA 芯片，这看起来就是一个挺大的漏洞。

turns.en: Yeah. So, I mean, the arrangement that Megaspeed has with Alibaba is extraordinarily common across the Southeast Asian data center ecosystem. You know, in some ways, the backbone of Chinese compute is like Johor, Malaysia. So it's not actually the remote access cloud computing arrangement that got Megaspeed sort of looked at by the U.S. government, later by the Singapore government. It's the suspicion that the company has not just rented compute to Chinese offtakers, but actually diverted those, like the physical hardware into mainland China. Right. So that's the focus of the U.S. investigation. It was looking at whether Megaspeed had smuggled chips, which the company has categorically denied having ever done. And also looking into its ownership structure, because even if Megaspeed is a Singaporean entity, if it were owned by a Chinese company, it would also be illegal to sell advanced NVIDIA chips to Megaspeed without a U.S. license. It is 100 percent Singapore owned, but by a shell.
turns.zh: 对。Megaspeed 跟 Alibaba 之间的这种安排，在整个东南亚数据中心生态里非常普遍。某种意义上说，中国算力的骨架就是马来西亚的 Johor（柔佛）。所以真正让 Megaspeed 被美国政府盯上、后来又在新加坡被盯上的，并不是远程访问（remote access）式的云计算安排，而是有人怀疑这家公司不只是把算力租给中国的采购方，而是把实体硬件转移进了中国大陆。这才是美国调查的重点：查它有没有走私芯片——这家公司断然否认自己做过这种事；同时也查它的股权结构，因为即便 Megaspeed 是一家新加坡实体，如果它由中国公司持股，那么在没有美国许可证的情况下把先进 NVIDIA 芯片卖给 Megaspeed 同样违法。它 100% 由新加坡一方持有，但持有者是一个空壳。

turns.en: Let's get into like there is this question of, you know, what do chip restrictions even mean if you could still just access a cloud in a different country? And like, is this the mother of all loopholes? But let's actually just start on the smuggling question. Why might investigators have been concerned that Megaspeed was literally smuggling chips or not? Like, what are the details that we know around this question? The actual, the physical movement of chips from, say, a delivery address in Johor, Malaysia to an address inside of mainland China.
turns.zh: 我们来展开说说。有一个问题是：如果你还是能去访问另一个国家的云，那芯片限制到底还有什么意义？这是不是所有漏洞之母？不过我们先从走私这个问题说起。调查人员为什么会怀疑 Megaspeed 确实在走私芯片？围绕这个问题我们知道哪些细节？就是芯片实际的物理移动——比如说从马来西亚 Johor 的某个交货地址，运到中国大陆境内的某个地址。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: So, I mean, the U.S. government has a handful of export control officers overseas, including in Southeast Asia. And when I say a handful, it's really a handful. It's like a dozen. They're going to more than double the number this year to 25. For context, you know, when we did our investigation into Megaspeed last year, I think I was on singular email chains that had like 50 Bloomberg people. So the capacity of the U.S.
turns.zh: 美国政府在海外只有很少的出口管制官员，包括在东南亚。我说'很少'是真的很少，大概就十几个人。今年他们要把这个数字翻一倍多，增加到 25 人。给你一个参照：去年我们做 Megaspeed 调查的时候，我记得我参与的一个邮件串里就有差不多 50 个 Bloomberg 的人。所以美国——

turns.en: Government.
turns.zh: 政府这边能投入的力量就是这么点。

turns.en: Hold up, hold up.
turns.zh: 等等，等等。

turns.en: Probably says more about Bloomberg.
turns.zh: 这大概更能说明 Bloomberg 自己的问题。

turns.en: All of us in this room have been on email change with 50 Bloomberg people. A little inside baseball here, but this is a real phenomenon.
turns.zh: 我们在座所有人都进过那种有 50 个 Bloomberg 员工的邮件串。说点内部八卦，但这真的是个普遍现象。

turns.en: All right, keep going.
turns.zh: 好，你继续。

turns.en: But no, in all seriousness, the U.S. government has fairly limited enforcement capacity overseas, but they do checks. And there's unfortunately not a ton that I can say about the initial trigger for the probe into mega speed. But through the course of looking at shipments through Southeast Asia, they thought that this company was worth digging into more. I can talk a little about why I started looking into Max Speed. Sure, go for it.
turns.zh: 不过说正经的，美国政府在海外的执法能力确实相当有限，但他们还是会做核查。很遗憾，关于对 Megaspeed 调查最初的触发点，我能说的不多。但在排查经由东南亚的货运过程中，他们认为这家公司值得深挖。我可以讲讲我自己为什么开始查 Megaspeed。——好，你说吧。

turns.en: If that would be helpful.
turns.zh: 如果这对你们有帮助的话。

turns.en: Yeah. So in April or May of last year, I had sort of recently arrived in Hong Kong and I was working with a couple of colleagues here and in the mainland on a story about this cluster of data center operators in China's western deserts that had issued reports procurement orders and local government tender notices that they had fulfilled to build data centers seeking 115,000 restricted NVIDIA chips. This was, you know, in order of magnitude larger than what anybody thought might be in China. And so a big question that we were trying to probe is, you know, it's one thing for them to be constructing buildings. You know, Chinese companies love to construct shells. I mean, I mean that physically in this sense, but obviously that is the case for shell companies as well. But it's one thing to build the buildings. It's another thing to put the chips inside. And so one of the big questions that we were trying to tease out that we weren't able to answer in that investigation was whether these particular operators had the supply chain, the black market supply chain necessary to get the GPUs. And when I was asking around in Southeast Asia supply chains, everyone just kept saying, look at this company called Megaspeed. And so we started looking at them a year and a half ago, maybe a bit over a year and a half ago. and found out, you know, several months actually into our own investigation that the U.S. government had been looking into them as well. The U.S. investigation remains ongoing in a sort of complicated way, which we can get into a bit later. In our reporting, we didn't find concrete evidence that Megaspeed had smuggled any GPUs to China. We found an extraordinary number of inconsistencies in their data center footprint that neither the company nor NVIDIA have been able to explain.
turns.zh: 好。去年 4 月还是 5 月的时候，我刚到 Hong Kong 不久，正和这里以及中国大陆的几位同事一起做一篇报道，讲中国西部沙漠里的这一批数据中心运营商——他们发布的采购订单、以及他们中标的地方政府招标公告显示，他们要建的数据中心需要 11.5 万颗受限制的 NVIDIA 芯片。这个数量级比任何人以为的中国境内可能有的规模都要大得多。所以我们想深挖的一个大问题是：盖楼是一回事——你知道，中国公司很爱盖空壳，我这里说的是物理意义上的空壳建筑，当然这话对空壳公司也一样成立——但盖楼是一回事，把芯片放进去是另一回事。当时我们想理清、但那篇调查里没能回答的一个大问题是：这些特定的运营商是否拥有拿到 GPU 所需的供应链，也就是黑市供应链。我在东南亚的供应链里到处打听，所有人都一直在说：去看看一家叫 Megaspeed 的公司。于是我们一年半前、也许是一年半多一点前开始查他们，结果在我们自己的调查进行到几个月的时候发现，美国政府也在查他们。美国的调查仍在继续，情况有点复杂，我们稍后可以细说。在我们的报道中，我们没有找到 Megaspeed 把任何 GPU 走私进中国的确凿证据。但我们发现他们的数据中心布局存在多得惊人的前后矛盾之处，无论公司还是 NVIDIA 都无法解释。

turns.en: I want to ask about those inconsistencies, but before we do, can you just describe how chip smuggling typically works? Like, how do people in the black market actually do this?
turns.zh: 我想问问那些矛盾之处，但在那之前，你能先描述一下芯片走私一般是怎么运作的吗？黑市上的人实际是怎么做的？

turns.en: Yeah, so, you know, we have enough examples of, you know, public allegations, things that are being actively prosecuted to sort of draw some thematic conclusions. There is a secondary market for NVIDIA hardware, but, you know, most NVIDIA chips get to customers via official allocation from NVIDIA. And NVIDIA doesn't sell chips directly to the end user, like they wouldn't be selling hardware directly to Megaspeed or directly to CoreWeave or whoever. They sell to OEMs, original equipped manufacturers, server makers like Supermicro or Dell or HP. Those server makers typically sell to distributors. Those distributors might sell to another distributor. then they go into a data center, and then they're often rented to another company. So it's this extremely vast distribution network for NVIDIA chips. But ultimately, in order to place an order and get your order approved by NVIDIA, you need to say, like, this is where they're going. Like, this is the customer, this is the data center location. And a consistent theme across, you know, what's now like half a dozen cases being prosecuted, and this is certainly the case in the indictment of Supermicro's co-founder earlier this year, The stated location of where the chips are going to wind up was not the intended location. You know, it's not that there was some sort of rogue person at one node in the supply chain that was like, yeah, I'm just going to grab them. You have companies or individual actors that place orders that are purportedly for a destination outside of China with the intent of diverting that hardware to China the entire time is at least the allegation that's sort of laid out in several indictments that And then it's a question of, well, how much work does NVIDIA need to do and do the server manufacturers need to do to make sure that the actual stated destination of the chips exists? And there are some cases where prosecutors have alleged the data center literally didn't exist. There was never a place for those chips to go. They were just always intended to go to China.
turns.zh: 是这样的，我们已经有了足够多的公开指控、以及正在被积极起诉的案例，可以从中总结出一些规律性的结论。NVIDIA 硬件确实存在一个二级市场，但大多数 NVIDIA 芯片是通过 NVIDIA 的官方配额（allocation）到达客户手里的。而且 NVIDIA 不会把芯片直接卖给最终用户，也就是说他们不会直接把硬件卖给 Megaspeed，也不会直接卖给 CoreWeave 或者别的谁。他们卖给 OEM（original equipment manufacturer，原始设备制造商），也就是 Supermicro、Dell、HP 这样的服务器厂商。这些服务器厂商通常卖给分销商，分销商可能再卖给另一个分销商，然后进入数据中心，之后往往再租给另一家公司。所以 NVIDIA 芯片有一张极其庞大的分销网络。但最终，你要下单、要让 NVIDIA 批准你的订单，你就必须说明芯片要去哪儿：客户是谁、数据中心在什么位置。而现在已经有差不多六个案子在被起诉，其中一个贯穿始终的共同点——今年早些时候 Supermicro 联合创始人的起诉书当然也是这样——就是：申报的芯片最终去向地点，并不是真正想去的地点。并不是说供应链上某个节点出了个失控的人，说'行，我顺手拿一批'。而是有公司或个人在下单时号称目的地在中国以外，实际上从一开始就打算把这些硬件转移进中国——至少这是好几份起诉书里列出的指控。接下来的问题就是：NVIDIA 需要做多少工作、服务器厂商需要做多少工作，才能确认芯片申报的那个目的地是真实存在的？有些案子里，检察官指控那个数据中心根本就不存在，那些芯片从来就没有去处，它们从一开始就是要去中国的。

turns.en: Wait, can I just, I'm a little bit disappointed. Are there no chip mules out there? People who are just like, I don't know. I have this vision of someone in a trench coat and they like open it up and it's lined with like, probably not H-100s, with black wells or something.
turns.zh: 等等，我有点失望。难道没有'芯片骡子'（chip mule）吗？就是那种……我不知道，我脑子里的画面是有人穿着风衣，把风衣一掀，里面衬满了一排排——大概不会是 H-100，可能是 Blackwell 之类的。

turns.en: Well, you know, it's funny that you say that because, you know, in one of Jensen's many denials of chip smuggling as an issue, he said, you know, the Grace black well system wastes you tons. You're not putting that in your backpack or pocket anytime soon. We reported a couple months ago that the U.S. government has been investigating a Singapore headquarter logistics company that literally specializes in tech hardware transportation through complicated logistics. Those are fragile systems and transported or is believed to have transported restricted hardware. And then it's a question of like, OK, if you're a logistics company, then how much is it your job to know what's in the package? So a lot of these cases also involve false declaration or allegedly involve false declaration, you know, putting on customs forms that it's just a computer server. Ambiguous what type of computer server. Sometimes random electronics, there was one case where, and this is a case where one person's actually pled guilty already, where they declared restricted NVIDIA hardware to be, quote unquote, adapter modules. This is a category of electronics that includes the thing you use to plug your phone into a foreign power outlet.
turns.zh: 你这么说还挺有意思的，因为 Jensen 在多次否认芯片走私是个问题时，有一次说过：Grace Blackwell 系统重得要命，你近期是不可能把它塞进背包或者口袋的。我们几个月前报道过，美国政府一直在调查一家总部在 Singapore 的物流公司，它专门通过复杂物流来运输科技硬件——这些都是很脆弱的系统——它运输过、或者据信运输过受限硬件。接下来的问题就是：好，如果你是一家物流公司，搞清楚包裹里装的是什么，这有多少是你的职责？所以很多案子还涉及、或者据称涉及虚假申报，比如在报关单上写'就是一台电脑服务器'，至于是什么类型的电脑服务器就很含糊。有时候写'杂项电子产品'。有一个案子——那个人其实已经认罪了——他们把受限的 NVIDIA 硬件申报成所谓的'转接模块'（adapter modules）。这一类电子产品里包含的东西，就是你出国时用来把手机插进外国电源插座的那个转换头。

turns.en: Really?
turns.zh: 真的假的？

turns.en: Adapter modules that weigh 2,000 pounds? So there are lots of cases where it's like, really? That's an eyebrow-raising declaration of But there are lots of colorful characters in broker markets. It's actually a very sophisticated black market. There are contracts. Brokers go and solicit hardware on behalf of specific suppliers. There was one broker who complained to us that the trade is so good and so many people are trying to get in on it. that now you have these scammers in the black market who are like purporting to have hardware.
turns.zh: 重达 2000 磅的'转接模块'？所以有很多案子让人一看就想说：真的假的？这申报也太让人挑眉了。不过中间商市场里有很多形形色色的人物。这其实是一个非常老练的黑市：有合同，中间商会代表特定供应商去四处张罗硬件。有一个中间商还跟我们抱怨说，这门生意太好了、想进来分一杯羹的人太多了，以至于现在黑市里都出现骗子了，声称自己手上有硬件。

turns.en: Oh, yeah.
turns.zh: 哦，对。

turns.en: Good, honest black markets.
turns.zh: 讲究诚信的好黑市。

turns.en: For like legitimate, honest black market brokers. No, it's a pretty extraordinary and sophisticated and sprawling ecosystem.
turns.zh: 就是说，为了那些正经、诚实的黑市中间商的利益。不，这是一个相当了不起、非常成熟、盘根错节的生态系统。

turns.en: Just one slight detail. You said that technically an entity like a Megaspeed or even a CoreWeave does not actually buy the chips from NVIDIA directly? And that actually the first buyer of the chips is the server maker?
turns.zh: 有一个小细节想确认一下。你说，严格来讲，像 Megaspeed 甚至 CoreWeave 这样的实体并不直接从 NVIDIA 买芯片？芯片的第一手买家其实是服务器厂商？

turns.en: Yeah, typically speaking, NVIDIA is not selling directly to the end user.
turns.zh: 对，一般来说，NVIDIA 不直接卖给最终用户。

turns.en: But the end user gets the allocation. So the end user, a CoreWeave, a Megaspeed, whoever, will get some allocation directly. that NVIDIA decides, okay, they're gonna get this many, but the actual chain first goes through one of the server makers like a Dell or a Supermicro or something like that.
turns.zh: 但最终用户是拿到配额的。也就是说，最终用户——CoreWeave、Megaspeed 或者随便谁——会直接得到一份配额，由 NVIDIA 决定：好，给他们这么多颗；只是实际的链条要先经过 Dell、Supermicro 之类的某家服务器厂商。

turns.en: Correct.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: Yeah, that's what makes NVIDIA the kingmaker.
turns.zh: 对，这就是为什么 NVIDIA 是那个'造王者'（kingmaker）。

turns.en: All right.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: Explain, as you said, this question of smuggling is not locked down, but you said inconsistencies discovered in your reporting. Let's talk about these inconsistencies.
turns.zh: 你刚才说，走私这个问题还没有定论，但你们在报道中发现了前后矛盾之处。那我们就来说说这些矛盾。

turns.en: On Megaspeed?
turns.zh: 关于 Megaspeed 的？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: All right, let's get into it. So, you know, one of the sort of first ports of call that I look at when I'm investing in a company for smuggling, which has now become a big part of my job, is do they have the requisite data center space? Like literally just the physical space in the building, the power supply to support the hardware that they have purchased. And we. Learned at a point in our investigation the number of GPUs that NVIDIA found when asked by the U.S. government to go and check Megaspeed's facilities, which they did several times. You know, they tabulated all of the chips across over 12 data centers owned by eight companies in three countries. They added up all the chips. They reported to the U.S. government. And around this time, you know, we got a statement from them in mid-November last year that said everything that was shipped to our partners is where it should be. We compared that number to Malaysian and Indonesian trade records that we had gotten and found that there were about 50,000 chips unaccounted for, which is like not a small amount of compute. And most of them were Blackwell chips, which at the time were NVIDIA's best hardware. And so we went back to NVIDIA and we said, you know, we're not talking about one or two chips that are missing. We're talking about a significant proportion of the overall hardware that Megaspeed has purchased. And after we asked about that, they went back to Malaysia and they said, oh, we found these warehouses that contain what's missing. And I said, OK, great. So we're going to subtract from the amount of hardware that we found in trade records and the number of chips that we know you guys told the U.S. government you found, and that should be the amount of hardware that's in these warehouses that we didn't know existed until a week ago. We have been talking to NVIDIA about this for a really long time by this point. This is the number, right? And they declined to comment on whether that's the number. I was like, okay. And then they eventually submitted an updated statement that said we've identified, quote-unquote, substantially all of the chips that Megaspeed had purchased via its hardware partners. And we'll do additional checks in the near future. So that was December of last year. I've probably asked NVIDIA 10 to 12 times over the past year whether those additional checks have occurred. I'm interested in particular in a handful of data centers. One, which is Megaspeed's largest data center, dropped the company as a tenant a couple of months after our investigation and a story by the New York Times that first broke the news of the U.S. investigation into Megaspeed. I don't know the reason that they were dropped, but if they're no longer a tenant and that's where a significant portion of the NVIDIA GPUs that NVIDIA told the U.S. government it found were located, that raises some questions about where that hardware might be now. We've not gotten answers to those questions. So that's one of the eight data center operators. Two of the others directly contradicted to us on the record NVIDIA's account of the hardware as described to the U.S. government. And so that's of the hardware that NVIDIA said it found in the data centers. And then you have this stuff that's, you know, in these warehouses. And we asked, okay, so NVIDIA's policy is, you know, we prioritize customers that are ready to put their products to use. They don't want GPUs sitting in warehouses for months and months on end. We asked, you know, what is Megaspeed's plan with this hardware? When are we going to see it installed in the data center? We didn't get answers to those questions. So that's just on the hardware side. allocation piece. Then we look at what Megaspeed has represented to investors and its data center footprint as the company describes it. And on its website, it had three data centers listed. We know that's an undercount of their total number of data centers, all in Southeast Asia. But in a presentation to investors in 2024, Megaspeed described five data centers across three countries and Two in Indonesia, two in Malaysia, and one in a specific area of an unnamed third country that on another slide of that same investor deck was the only one described as not in Southeast Asia. And the rendering that Megaspeed used to represent that data center is of a sprawling project in Shanghai. where Megaspeed's sort of Chinese corporate twin has been hiring engineers to work on restricted NVIDIA hardware. Companies that Alice, who has become sort of infamous in this scandal over the past couple of weeks, Companies that she has long-time business ties to have been investors in that data center. And so we asked, what's up with this product in Shanghai? Why is that the rendering that Megaspeed used to represent this facility on its investor deck? We never got answers to those questions either.
turns.zh: 好，我们展开说。我在调查一家公司有没有走私时，最先看的几件事之一——这现在已经成了我工作的一大部分——就是：他们有没有所需的数据中心空间？就是字面意义上，楼里的物理空间、以及支撑他们所购硬件的电力供应。在我们的调查进行到某个节点时，我们得知了 NVIDIA 在被美国政府要求去核查 Megaspeed 的设施时找到的 GPU 数量——他们去核查了好几次。他们统计了分布在 3 个国家、由 8 家公司持有的 12 个以上数据中心里的所有芯片，把芯片全部加起来，然后报告给美国政府。差不多在同一时期，我们在去年 11 月中旬拿到了他们的一份声明，说'运给我们合作伙伴的一切都在它该在的地方'。我们把这个数字跟我们拿到的马来西亚和印度尼西亚贸易记录做对比，发现有大约 5 万颗芯片下落不明，这可不是一个小数量的算力。而且其中大多数是 Blackwell 芯片，在当时是 NVIDIA 最好的硬件。于是我们回去找 NVIDIA，说：我们讲的不是丢了一两颗芯片，我们讲的是 Megaspeed 所采购硬件总量中相当大的一部分。在我们问过之后，他们又回到马来西亚，然后说：哦，我们找到了这些仓库，里面装的就是缺失的部分。我就说，好啊。那我们就用贸易记录里查到的硬件数量，减去我们知道你们告诉美国政府你们找到的芯片数量，得出的差就应该就是这些仓库里的硬件数量——而这些仓库的存在，我们直到一周前都不知道。到这个时候，我们已经就这件事跟 NVIDIA 谈了很久了。我说，就是这个数字，对吧？他们拒绝就这是不是那个数字发表评论。我说，好吧。后来他们终于提交了一份更新的声明，说他们'已经确认了 Megaspeed 通过其硬件合作伙伴采购的绝大部分（substantially all）芯片'，并且'将在近期做额外核查'。那是去年 12 月。过去一年里，我大概问了 NVIDIA 10 到 12 次，那些额外核查做了没有。我特别关注其中几个数据中心。有一个是 Megaspeed 最大的数据中心，在我们的调查、以及 New York Times 那篇首次披露美国调查 Megaspeed 的报道出来之后几个月，就把 Megaspeed 这个租户踢掉了。我不知道他们为什么被踢掉，但如果他们不再是租户，而那里正是 NVIDIA 告诉美国政府它找到的那批 GPU 中相当大一部分所在的位置，那就会让人怀疑这些硬件现在在哪儿。我们没有得到这些问题的答案。这是那 8 家数据中心运营商中的一家。另外有两家在我们的记录采访（on the record）中，直接反驳了 NVIDIA 向美国政府描述的硬件情况。以上是 NVIDIA 说它在数据中心里找到的那部分硬件。然后还有那些放在这些仓库里的东西。我们问：好，NVIDIA 的政策是'我们优先服务那些准备好把产品投入使用的客户'，他们不希望 GPU 在仓库里一放就是好几个月。我们问：Megaspeed 对这些硬件的计划是什么？我们什么时候能看到它们被装进数据中心？这些问题我们也没有得到答案。以上只是硬件和配额这一侧。然后我们再看 Megaspeed 向投资者陈述了什么、以及公司自己描述的数据中心布局。它的网站上列了 3 个数据中心，我们知道这个数字低估了它的数据中心总数，而且都在东南亚。但在 2024 年给投资者的一份演示材料里，Megaspeed 描述了分布在 3 个国家的 5 个数据中心：Indonesia 2 个、Malaysia 2 个，还有一个在一个未点名的第三个国家的某个具体区域——而在那份投资者材料的另一页幻灯片上，只有这一个被描述为不在东南亚。Megaspeed 用来代表那个数据中心的效果图，是 Shanghai 的一个庞大项目；Megaspeed 在中国的那个'孪生'公司一直在为那个项目招聘工程师，去处理受限的 NVIDIA 硬件。Alice——过去几周她在这起丑闻中已经有点臭名昭著了——长期有业务往来的那些公司，一直是那个数据中心的投资方。于是我们问：Shanghai 这个项目是怎么回事？为什么 Megaspeed 在投资者材料里用这张效果图来代表这个设施？这些问题我们也始终没有得到答案。

turns.en: It's such a weird decision to talk about, oh, and we also have this project in a country that we're not going to name, but here's an illustration of Shanghai. Yeah. OK, and just so we're clear, can you outline what exactly are the responsibilities of NVIDIA here? So if it sells chips to a server company and the server company declares that like the end user is definitely not a Chinese firm, is it incumbent on NVIDIA to like double check those claims or investigate? Like what do they actually what are they expected to do?
turns.zh: 这个决定也太奇怪了——'哦，对了，我们在一个不方便透露国名的国家也有一个项目，不过这里给你一张 Shanghai 的效果图'。是啊。好，为了让我们搞清楚，你能说明一下 NVIDIA 在这里到底要负哪些责任吗？也就是说，如果它把芯片卖给一家服务器公司，而服务器公司声明最终用户绝对不是中国公司，那 NVIDIA 有义务去复核这些说法、去调查吗？他们实际上被期望做什么？

turns.en: You know, this is sort of the central tension that has been playing out over the past year is whose job is it to know? So, you know, in the case of Megaspeed, NVIDIA told us last year we asked the U.S. government if we need to cut off Megaspeed and we were told no. In the case where, you know, Supermicro's co-founders alleged to have smuggled two and a half billion or sold $ 2. 5 billion worth of hardware to an unnamed Southeast Asian intermediary that then smuggled the majority of it to China. We've reported that that Southeast Asian intermediary is one of the most important AI companies in Thailand. That company is alleged to never have had the data centers to install that hardware. So a lot of people have asked, did NVIDIA check did Supermicro check. And actually, Supermicro did check, according to the U.S. indictment. They audited because the volumes that this Thai company was purchasing were so significant. They audited, but then they allowed the shipments to continue multiple times. I think companies are always going to say, tell us what the law is and we will follow the law. If you don't want us to sell to this particular company, then tell us we can't sell to that company. But I think the question is, are there red flags that are so obvious that if you have sort of any competent due diligence program, you should have seen that? This is it's it's a conversation that's sort of being actively litigated in Washington, shall we say. And NVIDIA has started actually in some ways to self-regulate. Um, you know, they have this like top tier of NVIDIA cloud partners, these sort of like stamp of approval companies that are totally, you tell the industry, like these are, these are our top tier, uh, these are our top tier partners. Megaspeed is, is one of them, is still one of them. It became one of them four days after it was incorporated in Singapore. Another NCP, its CEO is on trial in Singapore for, uh, document for defrauding server suppliers about the ultimate destination of hardware. And there was like a mansion seize that was the alleged approach seize of chip smuggling. The Thai company was like sort of the initial hardware supplier for the like national AI company, Sovereign Cloud of Thailand, which is the first NCP in Thailand. So you have like definitely this interesting set of connections happening at the NCP layer.
turns.zh: 过去一年一直在上演的核心张力就是：搞清楚情况到底是谁的责任？在 Megaspeed 这个案子里，NVIDIA 去年告诉我们——我们问美国政府是否需要切断跟 Megaspeed 的业务——得到的回答是不需要。再看 Supermicro 联合创始人被指控的那个案子：他们据称把价值 25 亿美元的硬件卖给了一家不愿具名的东南亚中间商，那家中间商随后把其中大部分走私进了中国。我们报道过，那家东南亚中间商是 Thailand 最重要的 AI 公司之一。据称这家公司从来没有可以安装那些硬件的数据中心。所以很多人问：NVIDIA 核查了吗？Supermicro 核查了吗？实际上，根据美国的起诉书，Supermicro 确实核查了。因为这家泰国公司的采购量实在太大，他们做了审计。他们审计了，但之后又多次允许出货继续进行。我认为公司永远都会说：告诉我们法律是什么，我们就遵守法律；如果你不希望我们卖给这家特定公司，那就告诉我们不能卖给那家公司。但我觉得问题在于：有些危险信号（red flag）是不是明显到——只要你有哪怕一套还算称职的尽职调查流程，你就应该看得出来？这场讨论，可以说正在 Washington 被激烈地'审理'着。而 NVIDIA 其实已经开始在某些方面自我监管了。他们有一个顶级层级的 NVIDIA Cloud Partner（NVIDIA 云合作伙伴，NCP），就是那种盖了'认可章'的公司，等于向整个行业宣告：这些是我们的顶级合作伙伴。Megaspeed 是其中之一，而且现在仍然是其中之一；它在 Singapore 注册成立四天后就成了顶级合作伙伴。另一家 NCP 的 CEO 正在 Singapore 受审，罪名是就硬件的最终去向欺骗服务器供应商；还有一栋豪宅被查封，据称是芯片走私的犯罪所得。那家泰国公司则大致是 Thailand 国家 AI 公司、Sovereign Cloud of Thailand 的最初硬件供应商，而后者是 Thailand 的第一家 NCP。所以在 NCP 这一层，你确实能看到一组很有意思的关联。

turns.en: The NCP stands for?
turns.zh: NCP 是什么的缩写？

turns.en: NVIDIA Cloud Partner. Oh, yeah, yeah.
turns.zh: NVIDIA Cloud Partner。哦，对对。

turns.en: Sorry, sorry.
turns.zh: 抱歉，抱歉。

turns.en: Sorry. Yeah, yeah. So there's also like an internal whitelist of companies that NVIDIA has sort of pre-approved for purchase. And after the Supermicro co-founder's indictment earlier this year, NVIDIA went and cleaved a lot of companies from that whitelist. And it's this interesting thing because on the one hand, this is the type of due diligence maybe that some Washington regulators would like to see the chipmaker take. On the other, it raises questions of, you know, On what basis did you remove those companies? Why were they on the whitelist in the first place? And so, you know, I think also for NVIDIA, which is trying in some ways to demonstrate to the U.S. that it does take this seriously, but also has so deeply lost credibility on this issue that it's like a little bit of a catch-22. And that's not trying to absolve NVIDIA of responsibility, just sort of explaining a political reality that the company now finds itself in.
turns.zh: 抱歉。对对。另外还有一份内部白名单，NVIDIA 算是预先批准了名单上的公司可以采购。在今年早些时候 Supermicro 联合创始人被起诉之后，NVIDIA 把很多公司从那份白名单里剔除了。这件事很有意思：一方面，这正是 Washington 的一些监管者希望看到芯片厂商去做的那种尽职调查；另一方面，它又引出问题——你是依据什么把这些公司移除的？它们当初又为什么会在白名单上？所以对 NVIDIA 来说，它一方面想向美国证明自己确实认真对待这件事，另一方面又在这个问题上严重失信，结果就成了一个死结（catch-22）。这不是想为 NVIDIA 开脱责任，只是说明这家公司现在所处的一种政治现实。

turns.en: This was going to be my next question because NVIDIA, I mean, the thing we hear constantly is chips are in short supply. Everyone is scrambling to get chips. There's so much demand out there. It's hard to fill it all. They can afford to be selective with their customers, right? Do you have a working theory for why would they even take the chance if demand is so strong that they could sell to pretty much anyone?
turns.zh: 这本来是我的下一个问题，因为说到 NVIDIA，我们一直听到的说法是芯片供不应求，所有人都在抢芯片，需求太大了、根本满足不过来，所以他们完全有资格挑客户，对吧？那你会不会有一个大致的推测：既然需求这么强、几乎可以卖给任何人，他们为什么还要去冒这个险？

turns.en: That's a good question. NVIDIA's primary arguments on export controls are about the market share, the global market share of AI infrastructure that is American. They sort of view Huawei, their primary competitor in China, as this sort of existential threat to U.S. dominance. And their arguments are basically that NVIDIA's interests are U.S. interests. And so, you know, when you talk about the question of remote access, you renting the use of NVIDIA hardware that Chinese companies can't purchase themselves to those Chinese companies. You know, that's a policy choice by the U.S. government. You know, a lot of people describe that as like, oh, it's a workaround of the export controls. It's the loophole of the export controls. It's legal. The U.S. has the ability to make it illegal and it's legal in the vast majority of cases. You know, for NVIDIA, that's a good thing because NVIDIA chips are filling all these data centers in Southeast Asia that in many cases wouldn't exist if not for the offtake demand from Chinese companies. It's the same reason that NVIDIA wants to be able to freely sell its chips in China. We need to be able to compete with Huawei on its own turf. A question that a lot of regulators have pushed back on NVIDIA on this topic is Huawei can't supply the world's data centers. We're so far off from a world of Huawei being able to supply the world's data centers. And so how existential is the threat of Chinese compute on the global stage or even within China that the NVIDIA sales are aiming to counteract? But I think NVIDIA is very focused on these sort of battleground or what could become intense battleground regions if China builds its own AI ship production capacity that they want to make sure that they're selling in these regions.
turns.zh: 这是个好问题。NVIDIA 在出口管制问题上的主要论点，围绕的是美国在全球 AI 基础设施中所占的市场份额。他们大致把 Huawei——他们在中国的主要竞争对手——视为对美国主导地位的一种关乎存亡的威胁。他们的基本论点是：NVIDIA 的利益就是美国的利益。所以当你谈到远程访问（remote access）这个问题——你把中国公司自己买不到的 NVIDIA 硬件的使用权租给这些中国公司——那是美国政府的一项政策选择。很多人会把它描述成：哦，这是绕过出口管制的办法，是出口管制的漏洞。它是合法的；美国有能力把它变成非法，而在绝大多数情况下它是合法的。对 NVIDIA 来说这是好事，因为正是 NVIDIA 的芯片填满了东南亚这些数据中心，而在很多情况下，如果没有中国公司的采购需求，这些数据中心根本不会存在。这也是 NVIDIA 希望能在中国自由卖芯片的同一个理由：我们需要能够在 Huawei 的主场上跟它竞争。很多监管者在这个话题上反驳 NVIDIA 的一个问题是：Huawei 供应不了全世界的数据中心，我们离'Huawei 能供应全世界数据中心'的世界还差得远。那么，中国算力在全球舞台上、甚至在中国国内构成的威胁，究竟有多'关乎存亡'，值得 NVIDIA 的这些销售去对冲？但我认为，NVIDIA 非常关注这些战场地区，或者说，如果中国建立起自己的 AI 芯片产能，这些地区可能变成的激烈战场；他们想确保自己在这些地区有销售。

turns.zh: 所以人们可以——至少看起来有可能——GPU 本身的需求并没有像 NVIDIA 所说的那么

turns.en: And that actually, like, let's say the bottleneck is in places to plug them in, that if you want to actually sell the most number of chips for the most number of dollars, setting aside these sort of broad market share questions, that actually the Southeast Asian customers are important if we believe what we've heard from other purchasers of NVIDIA GPUs, that they're available if you can plug them in. And then beyond that, how do the Hawks or the people who argue in favor of export controls into mainland China, that seems really inconsistent.

turns.zh: 你能给我梳理一下吗，这到底合不合法？

turns.zh: 还有，你说这不是漏洞而是法律本身，那这条法律的正当性何在？

turns.en: I mean, it's the internet.

turns.zh: 我们在讨论什么？这有什么关系？

turns.zh: 针对硬件的出口管制并不管云。对对。不，有时候是有点让人摸不着头脑。

turns.en: This is like an active, raging debate in Washington, to be fair. And, you know, one interesting thing that happened this summer. So, you know, after Kimmy comes out with K3, it's sort of, it's like, seen as like a second deep-seek moment almost. The science and tech advisor in the White House, Michael Kratzios, posts on X that the Moonshot team acquired Blackwell chips, which is illegal. It raises questions of why has the U.S. government not, you know, why does the Commerce Department not take any action if that's the U.S. government's determination? And also that they had remotely accessed these chips in Thailand. And a couple of days after that, the enforcement unit of the part of the Commerce Department that handles chip export control. So the people who are like, oh, you violated, like you smuggled, we're going to go after you. That unit started mapping where in the world remote access happens, which is very interesting because remote access is not illegal. And so if you're an enforcer of export controls, you know, why is that your purview? But they started sort of crafting this list of countries where that's known to happen and And, you know, there have been at a very senior level of the Trump administration, pretty intense debate over whether to impose such restrictions. There's also interest on Capitol Hill. There's interest in Capitol Hill in being more hawkish on a lot of these policies, but including remote access. It's, you know, this is sort of nightmare scenario for NVIDIA if remote access were to be restricted. It's also a nightmare scenario for some hyperscalers like Oracle that counts Chinese offtakers as a significant portion of its business. There was great reporting in the Financial Times recently about Oracle having a cloud computing arrangement with Tencent that then the Trump administration stepped in to kill, basically, even though it was legal. And so it's like, OK, are we just going to do this ad hoc? You know, they do a lot of things ad hoc, but we'll see. You know, there's it's an active regulatory debate. Like, you know, the answer to this question could change by the time this podcast airs, although I doubt it.
turns.zh: 公平地说，这在 Washington 是一场正在进行、而且非常激烈的辩论。今年夏天发生了一件有意思的事。Kimi 推出 K3 之后，这几乎被看成是第二次'DeepSeek 时刻'。White House 的科技顾问 Michael Kratsios 在 X 上发帖说，Moonshot 团队搞到了 Blackwell 芯片，这是违法的。这就引出问题：如果这是美国政府的认定，为什么美国政府、为什么商务部没有采取任何行动？还有，他们是在 Thailand 远程访问这些芯片的。几天之后，商务部里负责芯片出口管制的那个部门的执法单位——就是那种会说'哦，你违规了、你走私了，我们要查你'的人——开始绘制全球范围内远程访问发生在哪些地方的地图。这非常有意思，因为远程访问并不违法。所以如果你是出口管制的执法者，这凭什么属于你的管辖范围？但他们还是开始拟定这样一份国家清单，列出已知会发生远程访问的国家。而且在 Trump 政府非常高层的层面，对于是否要施加这类限制有过相当激烈的辩论。国会上也有兴趣：国会山有人希望在很多这类政策上更加强硬，其中就包括远程访问。如果远程访问被限制，这对 NVIDIA 来说基本上就是噩梦般的情形；对某些超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）来说也是噩梦，比如 Oracle，中国采购方在其业务中占了相当大的比重。Financial Times 最近有一篇很棒的报道，讲 Oracle 跟 Tencent 有一个云计算安排，然后 Trump 政府出手基本上把它掐掉了，尽管它是合法的。所以问题就是：好，我们就这么临时拍板（ad hoc）地干吗？他们很多事情都是临时拍板干的，不过我们走着瞧。这是一场活跃的监管辩论。这个问题的答案，可能到这期播客上线的时候就变了，尽管我对此表示怀疑。

turns.en: Well, OK, speaking of ad hoc, I mean, part of the scandal here is that NVIDIA reportedly intervened in the U.S. government's Megaspeed investigation and said, yeah, it's all good.
turns.zh: 好，说到临时拍板（ad hoc），这起丑闻的一部分是：据报道 NVIDIA 介入了美国政府对 Megaspeed 的调查，说'没问题，都是好的'。

turns.en: Yeah, they're cool.
turns.zh: 对，他们没问题。

turns.zh: 他们没问题，相信我们。你预期会发生什么？我甚至都不知道那项调查现在是什么状态，它是重新推进了吗，还是怎么回事？你觉得 DOJ 真的会去追究吗？

turns.en: Yeah, yeah. So I just want to clarify quickly on the sort of scope of NVIDIA's intervention. So this is reporting from like two days ago. And this is such an active story that I'm saying what I know as of 10.38 p.m. Hong Kong time on Wednesday. So NVIDIA's general counsel, a guy called Tim Teeter, called NVIDIA. the head of the Bureau of Industry and Security, like the export controls enforcement and the agency that writes and enforces export controls at the Commerce Department in late summer last year to inquire about whether BIS was involved in the detention of Alice, who we now know was, you know, having an extramarital affair with Jensen. But NVIDIA says that Tim Teeter didn't know that at the time of this call, called to ask if BIS was involved in her being detained in Singapore. she had been brought in for questioning and restricted from leaving the country as part of Singapore's own investigation into Megaspeed, which Megaspeed said recently had concluded this year with no adverse findings. So Tim Teeter called to ask about that. He later emailed BIS staff who were working on the case and asked to meet with one of them. And they forwarded those emails to Jeffrey Kessler because Tim Teeter invoked Kessler's name. He's like, oh, like Kessler said it was OK to talk to you. And this was like this is not normal practice for an export enforcement investigation. And, you know, Kessler said, continue doing things by the book. You know, the Commerce Department said, or a spokesperson for this agency within the Commerce Department said, you know, everything has been above board. But the sort of nature of the investigation and the ability of export enforcement agents to act in the weeks and months after this sort of saga with Tim Teeter was diminished. You know, and agents or people working on export enforcement investigations you know, we're restricted from requesting information directly from NVIDIA without getting Kessler's approval beforehand or routing it through him. That's a policy that's unique to NVIDIA. It's not how things operate with any other major tech company. You were told not to mention Megaspeed or Speed Matrix, the name of Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary and external communications. And eventually the Department of Justice, which typically pursues these investigations alongside BIS. So, you know, if anything is going to be turned into like a criminal indictment, it's going to involve the DOJ. The Department of Justice had been working alongside BIS for a bit on this case, ended up asking BIS to stop its efforts. So now that case is with DOJ. You know, I think my my understanding of the status of the case a few weeks ago is would be probably very different from where things are right now. There's obviously intense interest in this within the Trump administration on Capitol Hill. So, you know, it's funny, like a lot of a lot of what we're talking about now was known such a long time ago. You know, New Times reported on it. We reported on it. But it's got a new life, shall we say, in the past couple of weeks.
turns.zh: 对对。我想先快速澄清一下 NVIDIA 干预的范围。这是两天前才有的报道。这条新闻太'活'了，所以我说的都是截至周三 Hong Kong 时间晚上 10 点 38 分我所知道的情况。NVIDIA 的总法律顾问（general counsel）——一个叫 Tim Teeter 的人——在去年夏末打给了 Bureau of Industry and Security（工业与安全局，BIS）的负责人，也就是商务部内负责出口管制执法、以及起草和执行出口管制的那个机构，询问 BIS 是否参与了扣留 Alice 一事；我们现在知道，Alice 跟 Jensen 有婚外情。但 NVIDIA 说，Tim Teeter 在这通电话时并不知道这一点，他打电话是想问 BIS 是否参与了她在 Singapore 被扣留的事。她当时被带去问话、并被限制出境，这是新加坡自己对 Megaspeed 调查的一部分；Megaspeed 最近表示，那项调查今年已经结束，没有不利认定。所以 Tim Teeter 打电话去问的就是这件事。后来他给正在办这个案子的 BIS 工作人员发邮件，要求和其中一人见面。他们把这些邮件转给了 Jeffrey Kessler，因为 Tim Teeter 搬出了 Kessler 的名字，意思是'哦，Kessler 说可以跟你们谈'。这在出口执法调查中不是正常做法。而 Kessler 说，继续按规矩办事。商务部——或者说商务部内这个机构的发言人——表示，一切都是光明正大的。但在这段 Tim Teeter 风波之后的几周和几个月里，调查的性质、以及出口执法人员采取行动的能力，都被削弱了。做出口执法调查的探员或者说工作人员，被要求在事先没有得到 Kessler 批准、或者不通过他转达的情况下，不得直接向 NVIDIA 索取信息。这是一条只针对 NVIDIA 的政策；对其他任何大型科技公司都不是这么运作的。他们还被要求在对外沟通中不要提及 Megaspeed，也不要提及 Speed Matrix——也就是 Megaspeed 那家马来西亚子公司的名字。最终，司法部（Department of Justice，DOJ）——它通常会和 BIS 一起推进这类调查，所以如果任何事情要变成刑事起诉，就一定会涉及 DOJ——司法部在这个案子上和 BIS 并肩工作了一段时间，最后却要求 BIS 停止它的努力。所以现在这个案子在 DOJ 手里。我认为，我几周前对案子状态的理解，大概跟现在的情况已经很不一样了。显然，Trump 政府内部和国会山对这件事有强烈兴趣。有意思的是，我们现在讨论的很多东西，其实早就被知道了：New York Times 报道过，我们也报道过。但可以说，在过去几周里它又获得了新的生命。

turns.en: Yeah, so Megaspeed on paper is 100% owned by a Singapore shell company that is 100% owned by a CEO who is a Singapore national. We tried many times to get in touch with him last year. We were unsuccessful. In terms of where it got the money, this is a big open question. $ 4. 6 billion worth of hardware is not a small amount of hardware. It has a compute rental agreement with Alibaba. Alibaba, you know, the way that these agreements often work is a company will put sort of a prepayment, sort of a guarantee, like, hey, like, you know, it's like you put a deposit down on an expensive purchase. Like, we are going to offtake this in the future. So there are, you know, financial transactions between Alibaba via a Singaporean subsidiary of Alibaba's two mega speeds where, you know, the entirety of its Malaysia business was offered as collateral actually. These are transactions that happened a couple of years ago, but don't sort of fully answer the question of where it got all of the money that it did to purchase the hardware. But on paper, it is a Singaporean company, and I don't have evidence to the contrary.
turns.zh: 对，Megaspeed 在纸面上 100% 由一家新加坡空壳公司持有，而那家空壳公司又 100% 由一位 CEO 持有，这位 CEO 是新加坡国籍。去年我们多次尝试联系他，都没有成功。至于钱从哪儿来，这是一个很大的悬而未决的问题：46 亿美元的硬件可不是一小批硬件。它跟 Alibaba 有一份算力租赁协议。这类协议常见的运作方式是，一家公司会付一笔预付款、算是一种保证，就像你为一笔昂贵购买付定金一样，意思是'我们将来会采购这些'。所以 Alibaba 通过它的一家新加坡子公司跟 Megaspeed 之间是有资金往来的，而且实际上 Megaspeed 把它整个马来西亚业务都拿出来做了抵押。这些都是几年前发生的交易，但并不能完全回答'它买这些硬件的钱到底从哪儿来'这个问题。不过在纸面上，它是一家新加坡公司，我也没有相反的证据。

turns.en: Let's talk a little bit about, you mentioned Huawei, and you mentioned that Huawei just doesn't have the capacity, the skill yet to replace NVIDIA on a global level, probably not even at a China level, given the demand.
turns.zh: 我们来聊聊——你提到了 Huawei，也提到 Huawei 还没有那个产能和技术，在全球层面替代不了 NVIDIA；考虑到需求的话，可能在中国国内也替代不了。

turns.en: Among Chinese AI firms.
turns.zh: 在中国 AI 公司当中。

turns.en: Yeah, you know, Huawei's senior executives themselves say it'll take until 2030 to satiate domestic demand.
turns.zh: 对，Huawei 自己的高管都说，要满足国内需求得等到 2030 年。

turns.en: All right, so talk a little bit about, like, where are they on this process? And, you know, in AI, we're always talking about, like, are they six months behind, two years behind, whatever.
turns.zh: 好，那就说说他们在这个进程中处在什么位置？你知道，在 AI 领域我们总是在说，他们是落后六个月、还是落后两年，诸如此类。

turns.en: Like, tell us a little.
turns.zh: 跟我们讲讲。

turns.en: Bit about, like, where Huawei is in its fight, I guess, to be, like, a real competitor with Nvidia.
turns.zh: 讲一点 Huawei 在这场战斗中——我猜是要成为 NVIDIA 真正对手的那场战斗——所处的位置。

turns.en: Yeah, so, you know, Huawei is... is such a black box. It's the sort of preeminent competitor to NVIDIA in China. There are a handful of other companies, of course, that are, you know, a lot of in the same way that a lot of American companies are like designing their own chips. You have that same pattern among a lot of the Chinese companies. It's just a matter of like whether they can get the production capacity. You know, that's the constraint in large part because the U.S. and allied nations have restricted the flow of semiconductor manufacturing equipment into China. But Huawei has made material progress on its chips over the past couple of years. And you're starting to see Chinese companies become more interested in adopting Huawei hardware. You know, I remember actually coming on OddLots a year ago and I was like, you know, one of the things that I'm waiting for is like, is Huawei ever going to export Ascend chips, which are the name of its AI chips? And also, are we going to see, you know, a frontier Chinese lab complete a successful training run on Huawei chips? You know, right now you're starting to see model releases out of China that have what are called like zero-day inferencing capabilities on Huawei, which is like, this is sort of optimized to run best on Huawei hardware from the moment that we release it. But that's a very different thing from doing, you know, pre-training on Huawei. And, you know, one data point for this is, gosh, it's been a busy news cycle, maybe like a month and a half ago, two months ago, we reported that DeepSeq, had placed a very substantial order for Huawei hardware, 160,000 of Huawei's best AI chips called 950DTs for use at a data center in Inner Mongolia that DeepSeq is building as its sort of like next really, really large domestic computing cluster. Incidentally, this is the same location within China that the U.S. government believes that DeepSeq has installed NVIDIA's Blackwell chips. We don't know what the overall composition of compute in that data center will be. Huawei is not going to be able to fulfill that order for more than a year. DeepSeq is actually lobbying the Chinese government to pressure Huawei to speed up its allocation. It would be great for Chinese labs if they had this alternative source of supply, right? It's obviously the U.S. government. you know, obviously we talked about their Monaxis piece, but, you know, everybody would like to own their chips, or at least have them in-country. The U.S. government has made it very difficult to use NVIDIA. They would love people to use Huawei. It's a matter of whether they can do a training run. And, you know, at the time of our reporting, Huawei was planning on using these 950DTs for inference rather than training, even though, or sorry, DeepSea was planning on using Huawei 950DTs for inference rather than training, even though they were designed as training chips. And Huawei's overall production capacity of that hardware is in the low hundreds of thousands. You know, it's just orders of magnitude less than what NVIDIA is shipping globally. But you still have started to see Huawei make some export attempts. You know, I wrote about a couple of months ago as well that they had submitted in response to a tender from the Egyptian government to build AI compute for use by Egyptian defense companies. And it was a very small amount of compute. It was like 2000 ships, but they were prepared to offer their best ships. And it was like, when you're that supply constraint, it's like everything that you're offering overseas is something that you're not offering domestically. And so as a company, you know, Huawei has to decide like, you know, as important as it is to get more Chinese developers, you know, working on its ecosystem, because you also get the sort of like iterative feedback loop when you have AI companies training on your hardware that helps you make your hardware better. They also want to make sure that they have these footholds in global markets. It's the same strategy that made them sort of the preeminent telecommunications provider. And that, you know, the U.S. government watched that happen years ago when Huawei became extremely successful in 3G, 4G. And they want to avoid that happening with AI infrastructure. So actually, when they learned of this bid that Huawei had made in Egypt, they like gathered this consortium of American companies and they were like, counterbid. And, you know, a lot of these companies had never really thought of Egypt as an important market. But, you know, they had these conversations with the Egyptian government. You know, we don't know the outcome of that tender process yet. But it's just sort of an interesting, you know, Egypt is an interesting battleground for Huawei because they feel a little bit blocked or boxed out of the Persian Gulf because there were these, you know, big American AI infrastructure deals last year, which I talked with you guys about about a year ago, how controversial those were. And Egypt is sort of an anchor in the Middle East, also an anchor in Africa. So you're starting to see these battles play out. You know, the Malaysian government is seriously evaluating use of an earlier generation of Huawei Ascend chips for its sovereign AI capabilities. But, you know, it's important to remember that the volumes that we're talking about here are just infinitesimally small at this time.
turns.zh: 对，Huawei……实在是太像一个黑箱了。它是 NVIDIA 在中国最主要的竞争对手。当然也有另外几家公司——就像很多美国公司都在自研芯片一样，很多中国公司也有同样的模式，问题只在于它们能不能拿到产能。这在很大程度上就是制约所在，因为美国及其盟友限制了半导体制造设备流入中国。但过去几年 Huawei 在芯片上取得了实质性进展，你开始看到中国公司更有兴趣采用 Huawei 的硬件。我记得一年前我上 Odd Lots 的时候就说过，我在等的两件事之一是：Huawei 到底会不会出口 Ascend（昇腾）芯片，也就是它的 AI 芯片的名字；另一件是，我们会不会看到一家中国前沿实验室在 Huawei 芯片上完成一次成功的训练。现在你开始看到中国发布的模型具备所谓的在 Huawei 上'零日推理'（zero-day inferencing）的能力，意思是这个模型从发布那一刻起就被优化成在 Huawei 硬件上跑得最好。但这跟在 Huawei 上做预训练（pre-training）是完全不同的两件事。这方面的一个数据点是——天哪，最近新闻周期太忙了——大概一个半月、两个月前，我们报道说 DeepSeek 向 Huawei 下了一笔非常大的硬件订单：16 万颗 Huawei 最好的 AI 芯片，叫 950DT，要用在内蒙古的一个数据中心，那是 DeepSeek 正在建的下一个超大规模国内算力集群。顺带一提，这正是美国政府认为 DeepSeek 安装了 NVIDIA Blackwell 芯片的中国境内同一个地点。我们不知道那个数据中心最终的算力构成会是什么样。Huawei 要一年多才能交付这笔订单。DeepSeek 实际上正在游说中国政府，施压 Huawei 加快给它的配额。如果中国实验室能有这么一个替代供应来源，那对它们来说太好了，对吧？显然——美国政府那边，我们刚说过 Moonshot 那部分——大家都希望自己拥有芯片，或者至少让芯片留在国内。美国政府已经让使用 NVIDIA 变得非常困难，他们会很乐意大家用 Huawei。问题在于能不能跑得动一次训练。而且在我们报道的时候，Huawei 原本打算把这些 950DT 用于推理而不是训练——抱歉，是 DeepSeek 打算把 Huawei 950DT 用于推理而不是训练，尽管它们是按训练芯片设计的。Huawei 这款硬件的总体产能在几十万颗的低段（low hundreds of thousands）。这比 NVIDIA 全球的出货量要少好几个数量级。但你仍然开始看到 Huawei 做出一些出口尝试。我几个月前也写过：他们回应了埃及政府的一个招标，要为埃及国防公司建造 AI 算力。那是很小的一点算力，大概 2000 颗芯片，但他们愿意拿出自己最好的芯片。当你供应受限到那种程度时，你向海外提供的每一点东西，都是你没有向国内提供的东西。所以作为一家公司，Huawei 必须做取舍：一方面，让更多中国开发者在它的生态上工作非常重要，因为当 AI 公司在你的硬件上做训练时，你会得到那种迭代的反馈闭环，帮助你把硬件做得更好；另一方面，他们也想确保自己在全球市场有立足点。这正是当年让他们成为最顶尖电信设备供应商的同一套战略。美国政府多年前就眼看着这一切发生——当时 Huawei 在 3G、4G 上极其成功。他们不想在 AI 基础设施上再看到一次。所以实际上，当他们得知 Huawei 在 Egypt 投了这个标，他们就召集了一个美国公司联合体，说：反投标（counterbid）。这些公司里有很多从来没把 Egypt 当成一个重要市场，但他们还是去跟埃及政府谈了。我们还不知道那次招标的结果。但这挺有意思的：Egypt 对 Huawei 来说是一个有意思的战场，因为他们觉得自己多少被挡在 Persian Gulf（波斯湾）之外了——去年那些大型美国 AI 基础设施交易，大概一年前我跟你们聊过它们有多大争议。而 Egypt 算是中东的一个支点，也是非洲的一个支点。所以你开始看到这些争夺在展开。Malaysia 政府正在认真评估把上一代 Huawei Ascend 芯片用于其主权 AI 能力。但要记住，我们现在谈的这些量，在这个时点上还小得微不足道。

turns.en: So this is very much a live story, as you've been emphasizing throughout this conversation, and one reason why you're very sleep deprived at the moment. But what are you watching out for next? So we still we don't really know what the DOJ is going to do. And now we have this independent investigation going into Jensen and the spy affair at NVIDIA. What do you think is going to be important?
turns.zh: 所以正如你在整场对话中一直强调的，这是一条非常'活'的新闻，也是你眼下严重缺觉的一个原因。那你接下来在关注什么？我们还是不太清楚 DOJ 会怎么做，现在又有一项针对 Jensen 以及 NVIDIA 那桩间谍婚外情的独立调查。你觉得什么会是关键？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, look, obviously Jensen's fate is sort of important for global markets, for the industry, you know, what the board ends up deciding to do. I think from a policy and regulatory perspective, you know, this is a very unique moment in an administration that, generally speaking, has, you know, adopted a lot of the policies that NVIDIA would like it to. There is... rage, honestly, on Capitol Hill and in many parts of the Trump administration about the overall state of export controls. Obviously, this scandal with NVIDIA gives people a lot of things to latch on to. So you're starting to see these voices that have not historically been particularly active on this issue take great interest in it. And then you have this sort of baseline contingent of China hawks who have been upset by what they see as a lack of action by the Bureau of Industry and Security, that BIS, within the Trump administration on this topic and are trying to legislate some of the rules to at least like, OK, let's not roll back export controls more than they already have been. Let's put additional restrictions on semiconductor equipment shipments into China. Let's make sure that it's unambiguous that the executive branch has the authority to restrict cloud compute access by Chinese companies. And a lot of these measures are sort of going to be litigated over the next couple of months as part of an annual must pass defense package. So it'll be a really interesting couple of months on Capitol Hill. Obviously, you know, Democrats are taking Congress next year. I would expect a significant amount of oversight into not just NVIDIA, but, you know, the major players in the ecosystem. And then I think, you know, for Southeast Asia, which is a bit closer to where I sit, you know, there's been this sort of whiplash over the past couple of years where, you know, remember like the AI diffusion rule I mentioned that the Trump administration is not enforcing? So this was going to impose, you know, licensing requirements, meaning you need to get the U.S. government's permission to ship NVIDIA ships to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, all these places where, you know, we have these smuggling cases happening. And so actually some of the companies that are suspected of being involved in smuggling like massively ramped up their shipments right before those restrictions were set to take effect. And then they didn't take effect. And then the Trump administration worked on a regulation. They were like, hey, we're not doing that, but we are going to restrict to Malaysia and Thailand specifically. This was a draft rule that I read about in June or July of last year. And then they scrapped that amid diplomatic pressure from the Malaysian government. And then they worked on another replacement regulation that would have done global export controls. We heard about that in March, I would say. And that was withdrawn shortly after it was sent to other U.S. government agencies. And so, you know, for companies that are trying to build infrastructure in this region, you know, even the ones that are doing it completely legally, it's like, are we going to be able to get the chips? Like it's this constant sort of, you know, the U.S. government's a little bit the boy who cried wolf on this issue. You know, we have this intense scrutiny into mega speed. Asian banks sort of go through like ebbs and flows of how comfortable they are with, you you know, financing deals that have a significant amount of Chinese offtakes? Or like, what if the U.S. government does restrict it and then are suddenly, you know, left holding the bag? And this is, you know, one of the fastest growing, you know, AI infrastructure regions in the world. You know, the amount of compute online right now is like, it doesn't hold a candle to what exists in the U.S., but it is fast growing. A lot of companies are investing here and it's just under, yeah, an intense period of scrutiny. So it's, yes, that's the developments that I'll be watching. And then on the Huawei front, you know, Huawei is making export attempts. And I think, you know, the U.S. government, it's funny, like over a year ago, there was an executive order to promote the export of the American AI stack to basically like design these packages that you could sort of offer to you know, other countries of like adopt, you know, up and down, you know, from applications to models to infrastructure, the American AI stack. And we haven't seen like anything come out of that program yet. And now we actually do have Huawei like starting to make these attempts. And the U.S. is sort of responding to them on like an ad hoc basis. And I'm sure that we'll see more of that over the next year. So you'll start to see like these battlegrounds in the global south that will be really interesting to watch, you know, how foreign governments are make decisions about their own sovereign capabilities and whether they think, you know, the U.S. is a reliable partner or they're willing to take, you know, maybe worse trips from China that, you know, Huawei is happy to like send their engineers there and do the whole data center for you. And yeah, I know it's exciting times.
turns.zh: 对，我是说，显然 Jensen 的去向对全球市场、对整个行业都挺重要，也就是董事会最后决定怎么做。我认为从政策和监管的角度看，这是一个非常独特的时刻：这个政府总的来说已经采纳了很多 NVIDIA 希望它采纳的政策。而说实话，国会山以及 Trump 政府的很多部门，对出口管制的整体状况是愤怒的。显然，NVIDIA 这起丑闻给了人们很多可以抓住的东西。所以你开始看到那些历史上在这个议题上并不特别活跃的声音，对它产生了浓厚兴趣。然后你还有一批基本的对华鹰派，他们一直不满于 Trump 政府内部的 Bureau of Industry and Security，也就是那个 BIS，在这个话题上缺乏行动，于是他们试图把一些规则写进立法，至少要做到：好，我们不要再把出口管制往回撤得比现在更多了；对进入中国的半导体设备出货施加额外限制；确保毫无疑问地写明行政部门有权限制中国公司获取云算力。这些措施中有很多将在接下来几个月里，作为年度必须通过的国防法案的一部分被反复博弈。所以国会山接下来几个月会非常有意思。显然，民主党明年要接手国会，我预计会有大量监督，不只是针对 NVIDIA，也针对这个生态里的主要玩家。然后我想，对于东南亚——这离我坐的位置更近一点——过去几年一直有一种来回甩鞭子式的反复：还记得我提到的那项 Trump 政府不执行的 AI diffusion rule（AI 扩散规则）吗？它本来要施加许可要求，也就是你要把 NVIDIA 芯片运到 Singapore、Malaysia、Thailand、Indonesia 这些我们正在发生走私案的地方，都需要先拿到美国政府的许可。所以实际上，一些被怀疑参与走私的公司，就在那些限制原定生效之前大幅拉高了出货量。然后限制没有生效。接着 Trump 政府又起草了一项规定，意思是：嘿，那个我们不做了，但我们要专门针对 Malaysia 和 Thailand 做限制。这是我去年 6 月还是 7 月读到的一份规则草案。然后在马来西亚政府的外交压力下，他们又把那个作废了。接着他们又起草了另一份替代规定，本来会做全球性的出口管制。我想我们是在 3 月听说的。而那份规定在被送交其他美国政府机构后不久就被撤回了。所以对于那些想在这个地区建基础设施的公司来说——哪怕是完全合法地在做的公司——问题就是：我们还能不能拿到芯片？这就是一种持续的状态，你知道，美国政府在这个问题上有点像那个喊'狼来了'的男孩。我们对 Megaspeed 有这么强烈的审查。亚洲的银行在'他们有多愿意为含有大量中国采购方的交易提供融资'这件事上，也是一阵一阵的。或者说：万一美国政府真的限制了，然后他们突然就成了接盘的人（left holding the bag）呢？而这里是世界上增长最快的 AI 基础设施地区之一。目前上线的算力规模，跟美国现有的相比根本不值一提，但它增长很快。很多公司在这里投资，而它正处在一个高强度的审查期。所以，是的，这些就是我会盯着的进展。然后在 Huawei 这条线上，Huawei 正在做出出口尝试。我觉得，美国政府——有意思的是，一年多以前有一项行政令，要推动美国 AI 技术栈（American AI stack）的出口，基本上就是设计一些打包方案，可以提供给其他国家，让他们从上到下整套采用美国的 AI 技术栈，从应用到模型到基础设施。而我们到现在还没看到那个计划产出任何东西。现在反倒是 Huawei 真的开始做这些尝试了，而美国在以一种临时应对（ad hoc）的方式回应它们。我相信接下来一年我们会看到更多这样的情况。所以你会开始看到全球南方（global south）的这些战场，那会非常值得关注：外国政府如何就自己的主权能力做决定，他们认为美国是不是一个可靠的伙伴，或者他们是否愿意接受来自中国、也许更差一些的条件——因为 Huawei 很乐意把工程师派过去，替你把整个数据中心都做出来。是的，我知道，这是令人兴奋的时代。

turns.en: Mackenzie, that was fantastic.
turns.zh: Mackenzie，太精彩了。

turns.en: Get some sleep. Well-deserved. You're going to need it. But no, that was great.
turns.zh: 去睡一觉吧，你完全值得，你会需要的。不，这真的很棒。

turns.en: Thank you for staying up late, catching us up to speed on all this. And I don't think this will be the last time we chat.
turns.zh: 谢谢你熬到这么晚，给我们把这一切讲清楚。我觉得这不会是我们最后一次聊。

turns.en: And I appreciate your coming on the hotline.
turns.zh: 也很感谢你来上我们的热线。

turns.en: Yeah, thanks so much for having me. Always a pleasure, guys.
turns.zh: 嗯，非常感谢你们邀请我。一直很愉快，各位。

turns.en: She's so great. These are such complicated stories.
turns.zh: 她太棒了。这些新闻真是太复杂了。

turns.en: They really are.
turns.zh: 确实是的。

turns.en: They're really complicated. There's so many different... dimensions to them.
turns.zh: 真的太复杂了，有那么多个不同的……层面。

turns.en: Also, there's a lot of legal technicality in what can and can't be said, which I think sometimes people don't necessarily appreciate from a journalistic perspective. And she's doing that all on like, I think she said she hadn't slept for 70 hours or something. So that's pretty intense. No, it's a fascinating story. I keep thinking it feels like a big tail risk right now for the chip makers.
